subject: Biotechnology
title: Viral Vectors for Gene Therapy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Viral Vectors for Gene Therapy.

hook.text: Viruses are experts at delivering DNA into cells — gene therapy turns their invasion skills into medicine.

buildup.text: Adeno-associated viruses are small, non-pathogenic, and infect many cell types — the most popular gene therapy vector.

discovery.text: AAV delivers genes that persist for years in non-dividing cells — ideal for targeting liver, muscle, and brain.

twist.text: AAV can only carry about 4,700 base pairs — too small for large genes like dystrophin, which needs 11,000.

climax.text: Lentiviral vectors integrate into the genome permanently — solving the persistence problem but raising safety concerns.

punchline.text: Tame the virus, deliver the cure — vectors are gene therapy's engine.

quiz.question: What is the main limitation of AAV as a gene therapy vector?
options: It can only infect bacterial cells, not human cells
Its small cargo capacity limits it to genes under about 4,700 base pairs
It always causes disease in patients who receive it

details.summary: Viral vectors for gene therapy are engineered viruses stripped of disease-causing genes and loaded with therapeutic genes, exploiting viruses' natural ability to enter human cells and deliver genetic material. AAV, lentivirus, and adenovirus are the three main platforms for clinical gene therapy.
details.whyItMatters: Viruses evolved over billions of years to efficiently deliver genetic material into cells. Repurposing this natural delivery system is the most effective way to get therapeutic genes into patients' cells, underpinning the majority of approved gene
takeaways: Therapeutic viral vectors retain cell entry ability but cannot cause disease
AAV provides safe, long-term gene expression in non-dividing cells
Lentiviral vectors integrate for permanent modification of dividing cells

faq.question: How are viral vectors made safe for gene therapy?
faq.answer: All viral genes required for replication and disease are removed and replaced with the therapeutic gene. Essential viral functions for vector production are provided on separate DNA molecules in manufacturing cells.

faq.question: What limits the amount of DNA a viral vector can carry?
faq.answer: Viral capsids have fixed internal volumes determined by their protein shell structure. AAV's tiny capsid limits payload to about 4.7 kilobases, excluding some large therapeutic genes. Lentivirus carries about 8 kilobases.
